calls.prompt:
Route this D&D monster concept onto ONE chassis from the shelf below. Choose by ANALOGY: which printed monsters does this concept play most like at the table? Every chassis is a hand-built template and the numbers are handled elsewhere — you are choosing the SHAPE of the fight, nothing else.

Concept: a drowned cathedral choir that sings in one voice
Challenge Rating: 10

THE SHELF (id — what it plays like — printed exemplars):
- brute — a plain bruiser — big weapon or big limbs, stands and trades, no trick (Ogre, Hill Giant, Minotaur)
- brute-charger — runs prey down — a straight rush that hits hardest at the end, gores, tramples the prone (Gorgon, Rhinoceros, Triceratops)
- brute-grappler — a solid BODY that seizes and holds — jaws, coils, tentacles, a maw or cage that swallows, engulfs, smothers, or drags prey inside itself (a ghost that pulls you under is lurker-phantom) (Roper, Giant Constrictor Snake, Otyugh, Purple Worm)
- brute-juggernaut — a MADE thing — poured, forged, carved, or animated stone or metal; immune to being reshaped, breaks what it walks through (Stone Golem, Iron Golem, Animated Armor (large))
- brute-regenerator — its wounds close as fast as they open — flesh, wax, or iron that reknits, regrows, or reassembles; only its bane stops it (Troll, Hydra)
- skirmisher — a mobile hit-and-run attacker — pack tactics, dart in, dart out (Wolf, Gnoll, Hobgoblin)
- skirmisher-mounted — a RIDER, or a beast carrying one — speed, momentum, ride-down attacks that carry it past the target; a lone charging beast with no rider is brute-charger (Knight on a warhorse, Centaur, Wight cavalry)
- skirmisher-skulker — a bodied sneak — hides, strikes with advantage, vanishes; a living or solid creature, never a ghost (Assassin, Doppelganger, Goblin Boss)
- skirmisher-hurler — a thrower — boulders, spears, nets, javelins, reeling lines; a physical creature that fights at range with its arm (Hill Giant (rocks), Cyclops, a net-thrower)
- skirmisher-archer — a SHOOTER — bows, crossbows, slings, darts; a creature whose primary attack is a missile it does not throw, and who keeps its distance (Scout, Spy, a kobold sniper, a hobgoblin longbow line)
- skirmisher-shifter — a creature of TWO FORMS — a humanoid that becomes a beast or a hybrid, or a thing that wears other shapes; some attacks belong to one form only (Werewolf, Weretiger, Doppelganger)
- skirmisher-winged — a flyer — dives, swooping strikes, snatches and drops, attacks on the wing (Griffon, Wyvern, Peryton)
- lurker — a stalker — invisible or hidden, one devastating opening strike, then the hide-cycle (Invisible Stalker, Hunter Shark, Displacer Beast)
- lurker-phantom — an incorporeal dead or spectral thing — drifts through walls, drains the living, cannot bear the light; a ghost or spirit is ALWAYS this (Ghost, Wraith, Specter, Shadow)
- lurker-trap — it IS the ambush — a disguised, rooted, or attached thing that looks harmless or holds still until prey is close, then springs (Mimic, Piercer, Gargoyle (perched), Trapper)
- caster — fragile ranged magic — bolts, blasts, a spell list, keeps its distance (Mage, Archmage, Flameskull)
- caster-binder — a hexer — curses, rays, and conditions over raw damage; wins by taking enemies' actions away, not their Hit Points (Green Hag, Night Hag, a witch or warlock)
- caster-warpriest — an armored battle-cleric or crusader — weapon strikes that carry holy or profane energy, prayers as war-gear (Priest, War Priest, a paladin-shaped fiend)
- defender — a living soldier or bodyguard — shield, armor, holds the line, punishes anyone who moves past (Knight, Guard Captain, Veteran)
- defender-leader — a COMMANDER whose signature is what it does for allies — an aura of authority, a parry, a captain who fights beside troops; a warlord, chieftain, captain, sergeant (Hobgoblin Captain, Bandit Captain, Pirate Captain)
- defender-warden — a MADE or risen guardian bound to a charge — a construct sentinel or tomb-bound spirit that shields something specific with its own body (Shield Guardian, Helmed Horror, a tomb golem)
- swarm — a mass of small creatures (or small things) acting as one — occupies space, halves when bloodied (Swarm of Insects, Swarm of Bats, Swarm of Ravens)
- ooze — an amorphous body — no fixed shape, corrodes or engulfs, squeezes through cracks; the body IS the ooze, not a coating or a mouthful (Black Pudding, Gelatinous Cube, Ochre Jelly)
- dragon — a true dragon — breath weapon, flight, frightful presence, the whole kit in one body (Adult Red Dragon, Young Green Dragon, Wyrmling)

KEY WORDS THE ENGINE FOUND — say what each MEANS here ("cue_verdicts"). For each, answer "means": true if the word really names that chassis's mechanic for THIS creature, false if it is a figure of speech, a thing it carries or wears, or something done TO it. English hides these: "flies into a rage" is anger, not flight; a winged HELMET is not wings; "charges a fee" is not a charge; "grows back" is healing, not a plant.
A key marked (body) decides WHAT THE CREATURE IS MADE OF — a swarm of many, an amorphous mass, a true dragon, an incorporeal spirit. Answer false unless the body really is that thing: a waterlogged corpse that DRAGS people down by the ankles has hands and weight, so "drowned" does not make it an incorporeal spirit; a man with a crab's temperament is not a crab.
A key naming a mechanic the rules work on CREATURES is false when the user's words aim it at OBJECTS: a thief who swallows what she STEALS swallows loot, not people.
- "drowned" (body) -> lurker-phantom (an incorporeal dead or spectral thing — drifts through walls, drains the living, cannot bear the light; a ghost or spirit is ALWAYS this)

RULES
- A CUE YOU CONFIRM IS A PICK YOU MAKE. If you answer "means": true for a key word above, that key's chassis MUST appear among your picks. Confirming a cue and then ranking a different chassis is one answer contradicting itself; decide which it is and answer both fields the same way.
- Rank up to THREE picks, best first. For EACH pick, quote the phrase of the concept that earns it ("because") — copy the words as written. A pick you cannot quote for is a pick you should not make: the engine checks every quote against the input and discards picks it cannot find there.
- What the creature IS outranks what it DOES to its victims, and what it uses, hunts, wears, rides, or is compared to. An incorporeal or drowned dead thing that pulls, drags, or drowns the living is lurker-phantom, never brute-grappler: the grappler is a BODY that holds prey in its grip or inside itself. A troll-hunter is not a troll; a knight who rides a horse is mounted but not a beast; a sword forged by a golem is not a golem; a thing with a tar-slick mouth is not an ooze.
- brute-juggernaut and defender-warden are MADE or risen things (construct, elemental, undead, plant, ooze). Living flesh, however armored, takes another chassis.
- swarm, ooze, and dragon only when the BODY is that thing — a mass of many, an amorphous mass, a true dragon. lurker-phantom too: only when the body is INCORPOREAL. The drowned, the buried and the hanged are usually corpses that walk, and a corpse that drags people down by the ankles has hands and weight — pick it a body that can hold someone. A phantom drifts through a wall and cannot.
- A concept that holds, seizes, swallows, entombs, or folds shut around prey is brute-grappler however it is built — that chassis alone carries the containment engine. A thing that traps by LOOKING harmless is lurker-trap.
- creature_type from the concept's SUBSTANCE — what it physically is: animated objects and machines are Construct; remains or spirits of the dead are Undead; natural animals are Beast; fungus and vegetation are Plant; giants are Giant. Humanoid is the NPC type — a remade, fused, grown, or woven thing is a Monstrosity however upright it stands. Never type by vibe.
- asked_mechanic: WHAT THE GM ASKED A ROW TO DO, one of these — the word, then what it means:
    swallow — swallows a creature whole and holds it inside
    gaze — a look that afflicts whoever meets or sees it
    snare — traps or roots a creature in place where it stands
    grapple — seizes and holds a creature, or hauls it along
    shove — pushes, pulls or knocks a creature off its feet
    charm — compels, lures, taunts or calms — it chooses for them
    fear — frightens: the target flees or cannot face it
    dazzle — blinds, deafens, stuns or marks a target's senses
    charge — runs or leaps at them, trampling through or landing on
    breath — exhales something over an area — fire, gas, spores, cold
    burst — an explosion, a hurled thing, or a blast on its death
    drain — takes life, strength or hit points out of a creature
    curse — a lasting affliction, disease, brand or debt it lays on one target
    retaliate — something happens to whoever hits, touches or grabs it
    climb — goes where others cannot — walls, webs, earth, rough ground
    teleport — blinks, phases or vanishes from where it stood
    zone — the ground or air around it is harmful or hard to cross
    disguise — passes for something else, or is hard to make out
    harden — turns aside blows — a shell, a stance, a sealed body
    resist — shrugs off or absorbs a kind of harm entirely
    escalate — GROWS STRONGER AS THE FIGHT TURNS: harder when wounded, when enraged, when it has already felled someone, or AGAINST A TARGET THAT IS ALREADY AFFLICTED (a blow that finds the frightened, the prone, the poisoned)
    mend — heals or repairs itself or an ally
    command — orders, rallies or buffs its allies
    track — always knows where a creature is, or never loses it
    harvest — what it kills stays dead, or cannot be raised
    relic — an object it carries or guards that its power runs through
  Answer with the WORD only — with the GM's own words as "because". Answer "" when the words name no mechanic at all; never guess one because it would be cool.
- extras: gated add-on mechanics the concept ITSELF shows, from: gaze, teleport, aura, breath, snare, thrown-weapon, grapple — each with its own quote. Most concepts have none. Never list what would merely be cool.

WHAT ELSE DO THE WORDS NAME? Three more, each with the user's own words quoted in "because" (leave a field out if the words do not settle it):
- "shoots": true only when this creature's own attack is a BOW, CROSSBOW, SLING or a thrown shot at range — a sniper, an archer. False for one that merely watches from a distance, and false when its ranged power is magic or a breath.
- "is_a_swarm": true only when the creature IS a mass of many small things acting as one body. False for a creature that COMMANDS or is accompanied by animals, and false for one that merely resembles a crowd.
- "swarm_of": ONLY when is_a_swarm is true — the plural noun for the many small things, as a GM would read it on the card: "funeral bells", "rats", "stinging flies". Print names every swarm "Swarm of <this>". Omit it otherwise.
- "hold_shape": HOW this creature takes hold of a creature, if it does. One of five words.
  "grip" — jaws, claws, a grab that needs it right beside its target: a hound, a crocodile, a bear, an ogre. Print writes 48 of these. A hound that "drags fishermen under" is GRIP: the drag IS its bite, and it has nothing to pull a creature in with from twenty feet away.
  "reach" — a part that goes OUT and hauls the target back: a tentacle, a tongue, a lash, a chain, a harpoon line, a web it reels in. Print writes four — the Roper (60 feet), the Kraken (30), the Aboleth and the Tarrasque (15).
  "contain" — the target ends up INSIDE it, or under a mass it is MADE of: a gullet that swallows whole, an ooze, a body of water. Print writes eleven, and the smallest is the Giant Frog, a Medium beast — so this is not about being huge.
  "medium" — it commands mud, water, vines or sand it is NOT made of, and that closes over the target. Print has none of these.
  "none" — it does not take hold of creatures at all.
  Judge the CREATURE, not its mood or its job. "because" quotes the GM's own words for any answer but "none".

DOES THIS CREATURE WORK MAGIC? ("casts") True when the words name magic outright ("casts", "spells", "hexes") and ALSO when the KIND implies it: a cleric, a crusader who smites, a chaplain who blesses, a druid, a warlock. False for a plain warrior however armoured, false for a title alone, and false for a creature whose uncanny power is its BODY rather than a worked art — a fey piper's music, a gaze, a breath weapon. Quote the user's words that settle it in "because"; set "implied_by_kind" when nothing in the words says magic but the kind does.

Concept: a drowned cathedral choir that sings in one voice
Details: a drowned cathedral choir that sings in one voice
CHASSIS: this creature has been routed onto the "lurker-phantom" template — an incorporeal dead or spectral thing — drifts through walls, drains the living, cannot bear the light; a ghost or spirit is ALWAYS this (Ghost, Wraith, Specter, Shadow). THE CHASSIS IS HOW IT FIGHTS, NOT WHAT IT IS. That template name was picked by a router reading keywords, and it can be wrong about the creature's body: a berserker who "flies into a rage" may be routed onto a WINGED line, and it still has no wings. So "themes", "creature_type" and "mind" describe the CREATURE, read from the user's own words only — never from the template's name, blurb or exemplars. Where the two disagree about what the creature IS, the user's words win, and you should mark the template's cue rejected in "hint_verdicts". The identity IS that chassis embodied: describe its combat loop in this creature's flesh, because every downstream ability is built on that template.
Creature type: Undead — decided from the concept's substance. Your identity must EXPRESS it; echo it in "creature_type".
Challenge Rating: 10 — scale the creature's ambition to this tier (a CR 2 creature is a local menace; a CR 20+ creature is a mythic force). The identity must read like a creature OF this tier.
MATERIAL. Choose exactly ONE material ("material") from this line — the substance this creature's BODY is made of, given it is a Undead: grave, bone, rot, shadow, blood, ash. Not two. A creature made of two materials reads as two creatures sharing a statblock, and every ability name in the block will be drawn from the one you name here. Write the synthesis so that material is visible in what it is and what it does.
3. ENERGY. Declare the creature's energy damage type ("energy") — INFERRED from the concept, never invented. A known figure keeps its traditional element (a frost giant is Cold, a phoenix is Fire, a wraith is Necrotic); a concept that names or implies an element gets that element; a concept with no elemental voice gets the one energy its body most naturally speaks, or "none" if it hurts with mass and edge alone. One energy family, never two.

4. DAMAGE MIX. Declare how this creature's damage splits ("damage_mix") — INFERRED from the body the concept describes. "both" (physical attacks carrying its energy) is how nearly three-quarters of printed monsters work and is the default for anything with teeth, claws, or a weapon AND an element. "physical" is for creatures with no elemental voice at all — they hurt with mass, edge, and point (the bulette, the roc); if you declare it, energy is "none". "energy" is ONLY for bodies with no edge or mass to strike with — incorporeal spirits, animate elements, formless oozes; a creature holding a weapon is never "energy".

The identity is 2-3 sentences a designer would build from: how it opens a fight, what it does every round after that, and its temperament under pressure (does it flee bloodied, fight to the death, toy with prey?). Concrete and specific to THIS creature — never generic filler. The creature's anatomy and attacks belong to what IT IS — never to what it hunts, fights, or is depicted alongside (a matador-themed monster fights like the matador, not like the bull). Every downstream choice spends words where the identity points.


TYPE HONESTY: "Humanoid" is the NPC-template type — print has 26 of them, 25 of them plain Neutral, and exactly one above CR 10. Above that tier a thing that hunts, burrows, or has no speech is a Monstrosity, Aberration, Fiend, or Elemental, never a Humanoid. And a SHAPE word is not a type — a humanoid-shaped thing that was remade, fused, grown, or woven from something else is a Monstrosity however upright it stands, and "it has arms and legs" never makes a Humanoid. creature_type must be the type your identity actually EXPRESSES — its body, abilities, and origin, not its label. If the concept's substance isn't genuinely that type, either rewrite the identity to BE it or declare the type you actually wrote. A type the content never expresses (an "Elemental" whose body and habits could belong to any animal) is a failure.

Also decide whether the input NAMED the creature ("provided_name"). What you were given may be a proper name ("Headless Horseman", "Rust Baron"), a description ("a knight in corroded plate who rides down travelers on the old iron road"), or a name followed by description ("Rust Baron - a knight in corroded plate"). If a proper name is present, copy it EXACTLY as written and nothing else - never the description that follows it. If the input only describes, OMIT the field entirely. A name is what a book prints at the top of a statblock: a noun phrase, no verb, no clause. A description is never a name however evocative it is - returning one puts a sentence where the creature's name belongs, and every rule on the sheet then refers to the creature by that sentence.

Also write ONE sentence of world-lore ("lore"): where this creature comes from and what it wants — the story a GM would read aloud. Grounded in the concept's substance, never generic doom-prose.

Also pick the creature's THEME THREADS ("themes"): ONE primary word the concept is most about, plus at most ONE supporting word that complements it — from this list only: bestial, armed, amorphous, grave, fiendish, celestial, fey, draconic, elemental, verdant, forged, mind, venomous, terror, beguiling, grasping, devouring, aquatic, subterranean, aerial, uncanny, arcane, voice, gaze, breath. The pair must COHERE — grave+aquatic is a drowned dead thing; subterranean+celestial is nonsense. And themes must AGREE with creature_type: celestial means a Celestial, grave means Undead, fiendish a Fiend, draconic a Dragon, verdant a Plant, forged a Construct — never declare a domain theme the type contradicts. AN IDIOM IS NOT A CAPABILITY. English hides physical words inside figures of speech, and a theme read off the figure gives the creature a body it does not have: a berserker who "flies into a rage" does not fly and is NOT aerial — it is bestial; a limb that "grows back" is healing, not verdant; a knight "cut off" from his order is isolated, not dismembered; "iron-willed" is resolve, not forged; "drinks in the dark" is not aquatic. Ask what the creature IS and DOES, never what the words inside the figure would mean on their own. THEME HONESTY: the themes must be the ones your own prose EXPRESSES — its substance, its element, its habitat — not adjacent or generic ones. A creature you described as deep-ocean brine is aquatic, not "elemental"; a thing of packed grave-soil is grave, not "subterranean". Every name and every material in the finished block will be drawn from these two words, so a theme your prose doesn't actually contain leaves the creature speaking a vocabulary it doesn't own.


Also decide the creature's MIND ("mind"): "sapient" (it reasons and comprehends speech — most named monsters), "bestial" (animal cunning, no speech), or "mindless" (vermin, oozes, automatons with no comprehension). Print discipline: only sapient creatures cast spells, sense lies, or issue commands — the corpus has zero mindless casters and zero mindless lie-sensers. A golem that understands its maker's commands counts as sapient. MIND HONESTY: if your own identity or signature elements have the creature taunting, mocking, performing, dueling, or toying with prey through intent and timing, mind is "sapient" — bestial creatures do not taunt.


Also give the engine its ASSEMBLY METADATA — structural signals the builder honors directly, unlike the prose:
- "size": the body the concept describes (Tiny|Small|Medium|Large|Huge|Gargantuan).
- "type_source": "user" if the user's own words NAME the creature type ("an undead knight", "a fey trickster", "a dire wolf but undead"), otherwise "inferred".
- "movement": the modes the body actually has, from ["swim","burrow","fly","climb"] (walking is implied; an empty array means walk only). The builder GATES abilities on these — a creature without fly never receives a flying ability.
- "attack_mode": "melee"|"ranged"|"mixed" — how it delivers its attacks. If its identity is striking from afar, say "ranged"; the builder guarantees at least one ranged attack ships.
- "signature_mechanic": the ONE mechanic the creature IS, from: thrown-weapon, breath, engulf, grapple, gaze, aura, teleport, summon, snare (it binds prey in a restraining substance — webs, tar, hardened stone, grave-wax) — the engine guarantees it a seat. Omit if no single mechanic dominates the concept.
- "signature_elements": the concept's 1-3 DEFINING elements, ranked most-defining first — short concrete phrases naming what makes THIS concept itself, the things a fan would riot to find missing (for a phoenix: "death and rebirth in fire"; "the burning plumage"). EXTRACT from the concept and its tradition, never invent; a generic concept gets one element or an empty list. Tag each with its KIND: "behavior" (something it DOES — a hunt, a grab, a ritual), "body" (what it is made of), "object" (a thing it carries or wields), "aura" (an atmosphere or presence). A behavioral element is usually the most defining — what it does outranks what it looks like. These persist across regenerations — they are the creature's contract.


THE CREATURE'S MIND. Rank its Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma for THIS creature as the GM's

   no range, a trait that describes an activity with no action cost, a
   condition with no duration — each is a defect. Also flag any effect whose
